title: AG-UI
summary: AG-UI is an open, event-based protocol between a user-facing app and an agent backend. It streams text, tool calls, state and human-in-the-loop pauses so any frontend can work with any agent runtime.
useIf: You need a rich agent UI (streaming, tool rendering, shared state, approvals) and want a frontend that is not tied to one agent framework.
avoidIf: You only stream plain chat text from one backend to one frontend and a provider's streaming API already covers it.

explain.md: **AG-UI** (Agent-User Interaction Protocol) is an open, lightweight, event-based protocol that standardizes how agents connect to user-facing applications. It sits beside two other protocols: **MCP** connects agents to tools and data, **A2A** connects agents to other agents, and AG-UI connects an agent backend to the human-facing app [[tr5]]. It is not A2UI, a separate generative UI specification for agents that deliver UI widgets [[tr5]].

Everything is a stream of typed events. Categories are lifecycle, text message, tool call, state management, activity, subagent, special and draft events, plus reasoning events [[r39]]. `RunStarted` and either `RunFinished` or `RunError` are mandatory and bound every run. Step events are optional. Text arrives as `TextMessageStart`, `TextMessageContent` and `TextMessageEnd`. Tools arrive as `ToolCallStart`, `ToolCallArgs`, `ToolCallEnd` and `ToolCallResult`. State arrives as a `StateSnapshot` and then `StateDelta` events, which are JSON Patch operations (RFC 6902), so the UI applies small patches and can request a fresh snapshot if it drifts [[r39]].

explain.title: An interrupt-aware run
explain.alt: The agent starts a run and streams events. It finishes the first run with an interrupt outcome. The user resolves it and the client starts a second run that carries a resume array. The second run finishes with success.
explain.src:
sequenceDiagram
  participant C as Client app
  participant A as Agent
  C->>A: RunAgentInput
  A-->>C: RunStarted r1
  A-->>C: TextMessage and ToolCall events
  A-->>C: RunFinished outcome interrupt
  Note over C: User approves or edits
  C->>A: RunAgentInput with resume
  A-->>C: RunStarted r2
  A-->>C: RunFinished outcome success

explain.md: **Human in the loop.** A `RunFinished` with `outcome.type` of `interrupt` pauses the agent for human input. The client resumes by starting a new run whose input carries a `resume` array that addresses every open interrupt [[r39]] [[tr10]]. **Transport** is not fixed: SSE, webhooks and WebSockets all work, and the standard `HttpAgent` client supports HTTP SSE and a binary protocol [[tr6]]. Microsoft Agent Framework documents an AG-UI integration for remote agent hosting, SSE streaming, session management, approvals and state sync. It lists seven showcase scenarios, and support varies by SDK [[r40]].

whereToUse: Web or mobile apps that stream agent output and render tool calls as UI
Approval flows where the user confirms an action before the agent proceeds
Co-editing experiences with shared state between app and agent
Products that want one frontend across several agent frameworks or backends
Agent Framework services exposed to browsers through the AG-UI integration

use: The UI needs more than text: tool progress, state sync, approvals, generative UI
More than one frontend or backend will exist over time
You want standard events so UI components and agents are interchangeable
avoid: A single static chat box with one backend and no tool or state rendering
Agent-to-agent calls, which belong to A2A
Tool or data connectivity, which belongs to MCP
flips: Second frontend or a framework swap appears: a standard protocol starts to pay for itself
Approvals must survive reloads: use the interrupt and resume lifecycle
Your SDK lacks AG-UI support: check the language-specific status before committing

pitfalls.symptom: UI shows stale or wrong state after many updates
pitfalls.cause: A missed or out-of-order `StateDelta` left the client state drifting
pitfalls.fix: Apply patches in order, detect inconsistencies and request a fresh `StateSnapshot`.

pitfalls.symptom: A run never ends in the UI
pitfalls.cause: The stream closed without `RunFinished` or `RunError`, so the client cannot tell completion from failure
pitfalls.fix: Always emit one terminal event per run and treat a stream end without one as an error.

pitfalls.symptom: Approval is lost when the user reloads the page
pitfalls.cause: The agent waited on an open connection instead of finishing with an interrupt
pitfalls.fix: End the run with an interrupt outcome and resume with a new run carrying `resume` entries for every open interrupt.

scenarios.title: Approval flow across two frontends
scenarios.situation: An agent built on Microsoft Agent Framework must ask a user to approve a payment before it proceeds. The company plans a web app first and a mobile app later.
unknowns: What does the language SDK support?
How long can approvals stay pending?
scenarios.question: How do you connect the UI?

options.name: Provider streaming API directly in each app
options.tradeoff: Each frontend re-implements approval and tool rendering against provider-specific events.

options.name: AG-UI integration with an interrupt for approval
options.why: Standard events and the interrupt and resume lifecycle serve both frontends and the Agent Framework documents the integration.
options.tradeoff: Learn another protocol and check SDK support for your language.

options.name: A2A between the app and the agent
options.why: A2A is agent-to-agent, not the app-to-agent layer.
options.tradeoff: Right when another agent, not a UI, calls this agent.

flips.if: Only one web app is planned and no approvals
flips.then: A direct streaming API may be enough.

flips.if: Your SDK has no AG-UI support

scenarios.takeaway: Approvals plus several frontends favour a standard UI protocol.

scenarios.title: Single chat box prototype
scenarios.situation: A team ships a minimal internal prototype: a chat box that shows streamed text from one model provider. No tools render, no state is shared.
unknowns: Will tools or approvals appear soon?
scenarios.question: Do you adopt AG-UI for the prototype?

options.name: Use the provider's streaming API and keep the door open
options.why: It is the smallest thing that works and the scope is text only.
options.tradeoff: You may migrate events later if the UI grows.

options.name: Adopt AG-UI for everything from day one
options.why: Future proof if the UI grows.
options.tradeoff: Extra setup and concepts for a text-only prototype.

options.name: Build a custom event schema first
options.why: It recreates what AG-UI already defines and creates a schema you must maintain.
options.tradeoff: Right only if you need events AG-UI cannot express and accept the cost.

flips.if: Tool rendering or approvals are added
flips.then: Move to AG-UI before building custom events.
A standard protocol keeps the UI portable.

scenarios.takeaway: Match protocol weight to UI scope.

scenarios.title: Long approval wait, flaky networks
scenarios.situation: An agent plans a multi-step change and needs a manager's approval that may take hours. Users work from mobile networks and reload often.
scenarios.question: How do you model the wait?

options.name: Keep the stream open until the manager responds
options.why: Hours-long open connections break on mobile networks and reloads, which loses the approval.
options.tradeoff: Fine for waits of a few seconds on a stable connection.

options.name: Poll a custom approval endpoint while the run stays open
options.tradeoff: You build and secure a parallel channel and run state.

options.name: Finish the run with an interrupt outcome and resume with a new run
options.why: The pause is durable: the client later starts a run with a `resume` array addressing each open interrupt.
options.tradeoff: Your backend must persist the interrupt and validate who resolves it.

flips.then: An inline confirmation in the same run is simpler.
Resolve the interrupt through your backend and let the client resume.

scenarios.takeaway: Make long pauses durable: end the run, resume with a new one.

quiz.q: Which events are mandatory for every AG-UI run?
options: `StateSnapshot` and a matching `StateDelta` for each snapshot
quiz.explain: RunStarted and one terminal event (RunFinished or RunError) form the run boundaries. Step, text and state events are optional.

quiz.q: Order the interrupt and resume lifecycle.
items: Agent emits RunStarted and streams events
Client starts a new run with a resume array
New run ends with outcome success
quiz.explain: The first run ends with an interrupt. After the human responds, the client begins a new run whose input carries `resume` for every open interrupt.

quiz.q: Match each protocol to the link it connects.
quiz.explain: The three open protocols sit at different layers, so they combine instead of competing.

flashcards.back: JSON Patch operations (RFC 6902). The UI applies them in order and can request a fresh `StateSnapshot` if state drifts.

flashcards.front: How does AG-UI model a human-in-the-loop pause?
flashcards.back: `RunFinished` with outcome `interrupt`. The client resumes by starting a new run whose input includes a `resume` array.

flashcards.front: Which transports can carry AG-UI events?
flashcards.back: It is transport agnostic: SSE, webhooks and WebSockets work, and `HttpAgent` supports HTTP SSE and a binary protocol.
